--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.add_gnp_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Add an Erdős-Rényi G(n,p) random graph to the current graph. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.add_gnp_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Add an Erdős-Rényi G(n,p) random graph to the current graph. title: >- [Graph.add_gnp_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Add an Erdős-Rényi G(n,p) random graph to the current graph. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add an Erdős-Rényi G(n,p) random graph to the current graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L11377-L11517){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.add_gnp_graph( n, p, directed=None, seed=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![G(n, p) random graph](../assets/graphs/add-gnp-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three random graphs on the same ring of eight nodes for edge probability p=0.1, 0.3, and 0.5. Each possible edge appears independently, so the drawings gain edges as p grows (3, 8, and 14 here) with no pattern to which pairs are joined." width="100%"} Each possible edge is included independently with probability `p`. This model is useful for generating random graphs with a specific edge density. The method adds `n` new, unlabelled nodes and then flips a biased coin for every possible edge among them. In an undirected graph each of the `n(n - 1) / 2` unordered pairs is considered once; in a directed graph each of the `n(n - 1)` ordered pairs is considered, so `u -> v` and `v -> u` are drawn independently. Self-loops are never created. The number of edges is therefore random, with an expected value of `p` times the number of pairs, and the graph's density will be close to `p`. Existing nodes are left untouched and never connected to the new ones. G(n, p) graphs are the classic baseline random network, used for: - null models: checking whether a real network's clustering, path lengths, or motifs differ from what random wiring at the same density would give - generating test graphs of a chosen density for benchmarking algorithms - exploring threshold behavior, e.g. the graph becomes connected with high probability once `p` exceeds about `ln(n) / n` Every pair is examined, so the running time grows as `n^2` even for very small `p=`; for large sparse graphs with a known edge count, `add_gnm_graph()` is the closely related alternative. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes to add. The new nodes have no labels and get the next available node IDs. [p]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Probability that any given pair of the new nodes is joined, in the range `[0.0, 1.0]`. `p=0.0` gives `n` isolated nodes, and `p=1.0` gives a complete graph. Values outside the range raise a `ValueError`. [directed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[bool]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Leave as `None` (default) to generate edges according to the graph's own directedness. Passing the graph's own setting (`graph.is_directed()`) does the same thing. Passing a value that differs from it generates the edges as if the graph had that directedness: `directed=True` on an undirected graph considers both orientations of each pair (so a pair can get two parallel edges), and `directed=False` on a directed graph considers each pair once and stores the edge in one direction. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same `n=` and `p=` always gives the same edges. If `None` (default), the result differs on every call. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `p=` is outside `[0.0, 1.0]`. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~add_gnm_graph`) : Fix the number of edges instead of the chance of each. [](`~add_random_kernel_graph`) : Let the chance of an edge depend on the two nodes. [](`~add_random_partition_graph`) : Use a different chance within and between groups. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In the Erdős–Rényi model `G(n, p)` each of the `n(n - 1) / 2` possible edges is included independently with probability `p`, so the edge count varies with the seed. For `n=50` and `p=0.1` about `122.5` edges are expected, and the density lands close to `p`: ::: {#b04071fa .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_gnp_graph(n=50, p=0.1, seed=23) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges(), round(graph.density(), 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (50, 109, 0.089) ``` ::: ::: In a directed graph both orientations of every pair are drawn separately, so there are twice as many candidate edges and roughly twice as many edges: ::: {#56153592 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} directed = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_gnp_graph(n=50, p=0.1, seed=23) directed.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 230 ``` ::: ::: The graph becomes connected around `p = ln(n) / n`, about `0.046` for `100` nodes. Below it the random graph typically falls apart into pieces, and above it it's usually in one piece: ::: {#fd26b370 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} [ (p, ec.Graph().add_gnp_graph(n=100, p=p, seed=23).is_connected()) for p in (0.02, 0.05, 0.1) ] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` [(0.02, False), (0.05, True), (0.1, True)] ``` ::: ::: ### Below and above the threshold For `30` nodes the threshold is about `0.11`. With `p=0.05` on the left, the graph is in eight pieces, several of them single nodes. With `p=0.15` on the right, every node is reachable from every other: ::: {#4fb01783 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} sparse = ec.Graph().add_gnp_graph(n=30, p=0.05, seed=23) dense = ec.Graph().add_gnp_graph(n=30, p=0.15, seed=23) sparse.count_weakly_connected_components(), dense.is_connected() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` (8, True) ``` ::: ::: ::: {layout-ncol="2"} ::: {#89186976 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} sparse.plot(width=320, height=320, legend=False, seed=1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
